I could not derive this rigorously within the effort available, so this answer is a recalled value that I have not verified.

The conditions are as follows. A red induced $K_{1,2}$ is a vertex $v$ with two red neighbours $x,y$ such that $xy\notin E(F)$. Avoiding it means every red neighbourhood is a clique in $F$. A blue induced $F_n$ is an induced copy of $F_n$ in $F$ whose edges are all blue. I recall that Gorgol's work on induced Ramsey numbers of stars versus fans gives $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(K_{1,2},F_n)=4n+1$ for $n\ge 2$. I checked a few simple candidate host graphs, such as $K_1\vee(\text{disjoint triangles})$, and they fail, but I did not establish either the upper or lower bound for $4n+1$.

ANSWER: $4n+1$
